# Architectural & Layout Polish Review

Before we dive deep into the specific features of the **Learn Page**, it is crucial to ensure our foundational layout shell is rock-solid. A beautiful page inside a broken shell still feels broken. 

Here is my brutally honest assessment of what we are currently missing or doing wrong in the layout/navbar shell:

## 1. The Desktop Squeeze (Overflow Issue)
**The Problem:** As you correctly pointed out, when the desktop Updates panel opens, we translate the main page right by `360px` using `x: 360` in Framer Motion. Because the container is still rendering at `100%` width, its right edge gets physically shoved off the screen. 
**The Fix:** Instead of purely translating `x`, we need to animate the `width` to `calc(100% - 360px)` or dynamically adjust the `marginRight` / `flex` properties so the content fluidly "squeezes" without overflowing the viewport.

## 2. Scroll Chaining (The "Leaky" Scroll)
**The Problem:** On mobile, when the Updates drawer is pulled down (`85vh`), scrolling through the updates feed will eventually hit the bottom. When it does, the browser will start scrolling the main page *underneath* the glass backdrop. This feels extremely unpolished.
**The Fix:** We need to implement a dynamic scroll-lock. When `isUpdatesOpen` is true, we must apply `overflow: hidden` to the `document.body`.

## 3. Route-Change Persistence Bug
**The Problem:** Because the Updates drawer is managed by a global React context (`isUpdatesOpen`), if a user clicks a link inside the Updates feed (e.g., navigating to a specific article), the route will change but the Updates drawer will *remain stuck open* covering the screen.
**The Fix:** Add a `useEffect` listener in the layout that triggers `setUpdatesOpen(false)` anytime the `pathname` changes.

## 4. Unforgiving Desktop Breakpoints
**The Problem:** The Desktop Sidebar is hardcoded to `280px`. The Updates Panel is `360px`. On smaller laptops (like a 13" MacBook), that's `640px` of UI, leaving barely enough room for the actual page content.
**The Fix:** The Sidebar needs a collapsed "icon-only" state (`80px` wide) that expands on hover. We should trigger this automatically on medium screens (md/lg breakpoints) to protect the main content area.

## 5. Z-Index Warfare
**The Problem:** We've been hardcoding z-indexes (`1100`, `1200`, `1090`) on the fly. When we build the Learn page (which will have video modals, tooltips, and sticky headers), this will inevitably lead to visual collisions where a tooltip renders behind a navbar.
**The Fix:** We must strictly document and enforce a unified Z-Index scale (e.g., `Backdrop: 1000, Header: 1100, Modal: 1300, Toast: 1400`).

## 6. Lack of a Unified Page Header Component
**The Problem:** Right now, the `AuthenticatedLayout` just spits out `{children}` into a padded box. If we start building the Learn page, we'll manually build its Title and Breadcrumbs. Then we'll do it again for Trade.
**The Fix:** We need an `AppPageHeader` wrapper component that provides a unified Title, sub-navigation tabs, and primary action buttons across every top-level route.

# The Block-to-Card Export Engine

This plan outlines the architecture for the "Quote-Card Generator," designed to weaponize screenshot culture and turn readers into micro-publishers via social distribution.

## User Review Required

> [!NOTE]
> This is a brilliant viral loop. Between the two technical options you provided, I strongly recommend we use **Server-Side Edge Generation (The Pro Way)** via Next.js's built-in `next/og` library (powered by Satori). 
> 
> *Client-side rendering (html2canvas)* is notoriously buggy on mobile Safari, often fails to render custom web fonts properly, and can freeze the UI on older phones. *Server-Side Generation* generates a flawless, high-resolution `.png` on Vercel's edge network in milliseconds, ensuring pixel-perfect branding every time.
>
> **Do you approve of going with the Server-Side Edge Generation approach?**

---

## 1. The Server-Side Generation Endpoint (`/api/og/card`)

We will create a dedicated Next.js Route Handler at `app/api/og/card/route.tsx`.

**How it works:**
1. The frontend passes parameters via URL search params:
   - `title`: The Spiky Title of the article.
   - `blockText`: The text of the block (e.g. the killer stat).
   - `userName`: The commenter's name.
   - `userRole`: The commenter's title/role.
   - `comment`: The actual comment text.
2. The endpoint dynamically constructs an HTML/JSX template using Satori.
3. It renders the 4 specific layers: Header (Logo + Title), Meat (Block Text), User's Take (Comment + Profile Pic), and The Hook (QR Code + Link).
4. It returns a high-resolution `.png` image.

## 2. The Post-Comment Flow (The UI)

To fulfill the zero-friction acquisition loop:

1. A user taps a block's Anchor Question and types their comment in the micro-forum drawer.
2. They click "Submit".
3. **The Hook:** The moment the comment is successfully saved, a beautiful `<QuoteCardModal />` immediately pops up.
4. The modal says: *"Brilliant take. Your peers on LinkedIn would love to see this. Download your card below."*
5. The modal displays a preview of the generated image (fetching from `/api/og/card?...`).
6. A large "Download Image" button triggers an automatic download of the `.png` to their device camera roll.

# Quote-Card Generator Implementation Plan

This plan details the technical architecture for the "Quote-Card" Generator, which allows authors and readers to export pedgagocial blocks into branded, highly-shareable social media graphics.

## Goal
To implement a high-fidelity visual export system that transforms structured learning blocks (e.g. Pull Quotes, Executive Summaries, Bionic Text) into stylized, branded PNGs optimized for social media platforms (Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram).

## Proposed Approach

We will build a dedicated client-side renderer that takes a block's data, applies the tenant's brand guidelines, and renders a hidden or overlaid HTML canvas. We will then capture it using `html2canvas` or a similar DOM-to-image utility.

### 1. The `QuoteCardRenderer` Component
We will create a new component `QuoteCardRenderer.tsx` that will:
- Accept a `block` object, `tenant` metadata, and an optional `aspectRatio` (e.g. 1:1, 16:9, 4:5).
- Output visually striking HTML/CSS specific to the block type (e.g., large stylized quotes for `pull_quote`, sleek lists for `exec_summary`, visual emphasis for `core_interactive`).
- Include the tenant logo, a subtle watermarked background pattern, and proper typography hierarchy.

### 2. Export Mechanism & Post-Share Modal
- We will integrate an `html2canvas` capture function to convert the DOM node of the `QuoteCardRenderer` into a high-res PNG.
- We will build a **Post-Share Modal** (`ShareOutcomeModal.tsx`) that triggers after successful generation. It will preview the generated image, offer a "Download PNG" button, and optionally implement the Web Share API for mobile devices.

### 3. Integration with the Form
- Add a "Generate Social Card" action button to the block cards (likely on the front face, near the edit/delete controls, or accessible when hovering over the block).
- When clicked, it will spawn a full-screen preview modal where the user can tweak the aspect ratio or background style before hitting "Export".

## Required Changes

### [NEW] `components/features/QuoteCardRenderer.tsx`

# Implementation Plan: Block Upgrades & Notion-Style Comments

This plan outlines how we will rebuild the editor interfaces for the Intelligence Blocks to match our new specs, and how we will lay the foundation for Notion-style inline commenting.

## 1. Block Editor Upgrades (The Writer Experience)

We need to modify the block rendering loop in `CreateLearnContentForm.tsx` so that when a user flips a block to edit it, they see the new guided fields.

### A. The Spiky Title (`subheading`)
- **Current State:** A single `<TextField label="Subheading text" />`.
- **Implementation:** We will create a "Mad-Libs" template selector. When editing this block, the user will see 3 pre-written templates based on the selected Era (Past, Present, or Future). 
  - They click a template, which populates the text field with `[Bracketed]` placeholders.
  - They replace the placeholders with their own text.

### B. The TL;DR (`exec_summary`)
- **Current State:** A dynamic list of generic bullet points.
- **Implementation:** We will restrict it to exactly 3 distinct TextFields. We will use the `SOP_FRAMEWORKS` definitions to inject specific placeholder text for each field (e.g., if it's "The Autopsy", Field 1 says "The Original Promise", Field 2 says "The Friction Point", Field 3 says "The Loss").

### C. The Disconnect (`myth_fact`)
- **Current State:** Only accepts one Myth and one Fact.
- **Implementation:** We will update the internal state of the block to accept an array of pairs: `content: { pairs: [{ myth: '', fact: '' }] }`. We'll add an "Add Another Pair" button inside the editor for this block.

### D. The Deep Analysis (`core_interactive`)
- **Current State:** A single `bionicText` field.
- **Implementation:** We will add a `heading` text field, and expand the main text area into a large multi-line text field. We will also add a dedicated field at the bottom labeled **"Anchor Question (For Comments)"**.

### E. The Ground Truth (`pull_quote`)
- **Current State:** `quote` and `author` fields.
- **Implementation:** Add an optional `avatarUrl` text field. When rendered in the live preview, we will display a sleek circular avatar next to the author's name if a URL is provided.

### F. External Data (`data_embed`)
- **Current State:** Placeholder block.
- **Implementation:** Add a `TextField` for an `iframe` snippet or embed URL. In the Live Preview, we will attempt to parse the URL and render a live iframe.

---

## 2. Notion-Style Inline Comments (The Reader Experience)

To support Notion-style comments without building out the entire database schema right now, we need to embed the "hooks" for comments into the blocks themselves.

### Implementation Steps
1. **Comment Hooks:** We will update our `BlockType` definitions so that `core_interactive`, `myth_fact`, `pull_quote`, and `live_poll` have an internal `allowComments: true` flag.
2. **The Prompt Field:** For these specific blocks, the editor will show a text field: **"Discussion Prompt (Optional)"**. 
  - If the author types a prompt, that becomes the dynamic question.
  - If left blank, we fall back to a generic question based on the block type.
3. **The Notion-Style Trigger (Live Preview):** Inside the Live Preview panel (and eventually the live article page), any block with `allowComments: true` will render a subtle **"💬 Discuss"** chip floating on the right side of the block.
4. **The Modal Drawer:** Clicking the "💬 Discuss" chip will trigger a slide-out drawer. At the top of the drawer, it will prominently display the **Discussion Prompt** (either dynamic or generic) to anchor the debate, followed by the comments feed.

---

> **Backend Synchronization**  
> We are significantly changing the shape of the `content` object for these blocks (e.g., changing `myth_fact` from an object to an array of objects). This might require updating the backend API validation if the backend strictly validates block contents. Is the backend flexible with `JSON` payloads for block content, or do we need to update the database schema?

> Allowing raw iframes can be a security risk (XSS). For the `data_embed` block, should we restrict it to specific domains (e.g., only `tradingview.com`, `youtube.com`, `dune.com`), or just allow any valid URL to be iframed?

## Proposed Changes

We will apply several crucial UX enhancements to `CreateLearnContentForm.tsx`.

### 1. Local Image Uploads (Replacing URL-only)
Currently, blocks like `highlight_card`, `media`, and `pull_quote` only accept external URLs for images.
- **Action:** We will import and use the existing `useCloudinaryUpload` hook.
- **Implementation:** We will add a small hidden `<input type="file" />` accompanied by an "Upload Image" icon button next to the existing URL text fields. When a user selects a file, it will upload securely to Cloudinary and automatically populate the URL field with the resulting `secure_url`. This allows users to either paste an existing URL or upload their own image seamlessly.

### 2. Auto-Scroll to Active Block
When a user has a long list of blocks and clicks "Edit" to flip a block open, it can sometimes get lost off-screen.
- **Action:** Add a `useEffect` hook that listens for changes to the `expandedBlockId` state.
- **Implementation:** When `expandedBlockId` changes to a valid block ID, we will find the DOM element using `document.getElementById(expandedBlockId)` and trigger `.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'center' })`. This guarantees the active block is always dead center on the screen.

### 3. Clear State of Completion
Users need a visual cue to know if a block is fully fleshed out before publishing.
- **Action:** Introduce a `isBlockComplete(block)` helper function.
- **Implementation:** This function will evaluate if the required fields for a specific block type are truthy (e.g., `core_interactive` needs `bionicText`, `myth_fact` needs at least one pair fully filled). If a block is completed, its collapsed card view will display a green `✅ Completed` badge, and its border color will subtly change to indicate readiness.

### 4. Minimizable Live Preview
The Live Preview pane currently takes up almost half the screen on desktop, which can make the editor feel cramped during deep writing sessions.
- **Action:** Add a toggle state `showPreviewPane` (defaulting to `true`).
- **Implementation:** We will add a toggle button (e.g., a "Hide Preview" / "Show Preview" floating button or header icon). When hidden, the Live Preview pane collapses completely, allowing the block editor to expand and utilize the extra screen real estate for distraction-free writing.

# Interactive Evidence Carousel Plan

You brought up two excellent points. First, the bug: the gallery counts "empty" images being drafted in the form, which breaks the `isSingle` logic. We will fix that immediately by filtering out empty items before rendering.

Second, the interactive carousel design. Moving from a basic scroll to a dynamic, "focus-state" carousel will make this feel extremely premium.

## Proposed Design Approach

We will build a **Focus-State Horizontal Carousel**.

### 1. The Active Focus Design
- **Active Card:** The card currently in the center of the viewport will be the "Active" one. It will be full size (scale: 1), fully opaque, and will display its caption and source text cleanly below it.
- **Inactive Cards:** Cards on the left and right will scale down slightly (e.g., `scale: 0.85`), drop in opacity (e.g., `0.5`), and take on a very subtle tilt (`rotate: -2deg` or `2deg` depending on their position). 
- **Text Visibility:** The caption and credits will fade out entirely for inactive cards, keeping the interface clean and drawing the eye instantly to the active image.

### 2. Smooth Centering & Pagination
- The scroll container will have padding on the left and right so that the very first and very last cards can be perfectly centered on the screen.
- The numbered pagination dots will map directly to the active index.
- Tapping a pagination dot will smoothly scroll that specific card to the exact center of the screen, triggering its active "slide out/scale up" animation while the previous one shrinks back into the stack.

### 3. The Empty Item Bug
- We will define `validItems = items.filter(item => item.url)` at the top of the component. All rendering, sizing logic, and single-item banner logic will be based *only* on valid items.
